title: Forty Tabs, One Cart
subtitle: 6 a.m. on Black Friday. Sam has forty deal tabs open. Jo has a rule.
end: What is actually selling, and the price that makes each deal real: the list is below.
style: Black Friday morning palette: dark blue dawn outside, warm lamp and screen glow inside, pops of red sale color.

art.prompt: 6 a.m., still dark blue outside the window: Sam sits cross-legged on his sofa in a hoodie with a laptop and a phone, both screens crowded with abstract red-and-yellow sale tiles (nothing readable), coffee mug steaming, Biscuit asleep on a cushion. Comic, cozy, slightly overwhelmed. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Forty tabs. Every single one says DEAL.

art.prompt: Jo, in a coat with snow on her shoulders, leans over the back of the sofa holding a takeaway coffee and points at Sam's laptop with a knowing smile; Sam looks up at her, startled. Warm lamp light. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Americans spent $7.1 billion online on Thanksgiving alone, says Adobe.

art.prompt: Comic extreme close-up of Sam's shocked face, eyes huge, coffee mid-spill, manga speed lines radiating behind him. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Sources: Adobe via USA Today; Walmart's merchandising chief via Fox Business; Circana via VGChartz.

art.prompt: Vera bursts into frame through a shower of falling red sale tags and confetti, one finger raised like a referee calling a foul, confident grin, dynamic pose. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Popular isn't the same as cheap.
Check one thing before you click: the model number.

art.prompt: Vera stands between two big generic flat TV boxes that look almost identical (blank boxes, no logos), tapping one box's small blank label with a pen, like a detective. Bright store aisle. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Some doorbuster TVs are store-only versions with their own model numbers. Compare the model number, not the box.

items.title: Buy today or wait for Cyber Monday?

items.text: Adobe's 2026 forecast of the best day for each category (Sept 28, 2026).

art.prompt: Jo and Sam side by side on the sofa looking at one phone together, Jo pointing at a simple line chart of a price dropping (no numbers or words), Sam nodding, both focused and amused. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: Our rule: it's a deal only at or under its past low.

art.prompt: Morning sun now streaming in: Sam closes the laptop triumphantly while Jo high-fives him; Biscuit jumps up wagging; one small cart icon glows on the phone screen (no text). Joyful, warm, funny ending. Full-bleed single image, edge to edge, no split frames.

items.text: One cart. Three things. Zero regret.
